newsitem.title: MEXICO: INTERVIEW-Pemex bumps up BA paper on heavy demand.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Pemex bumps up BA paper on heavy demand.

text.p: Mexican oil company Petroleos Mexicanos bumped up the size of its two recently renewed bankers acceptance programs due to strong demand, Pemex chief financial officer Juan Manuel Romero said.
"What we have seen with our renewals is that...they have been over-subscribed. We have had placements above the limits that we set," Romero said in an interview with Reuters.
"We have had very successful renewals in both commercial paper as well as in bankers acceptances," he added.
Demand for the one BA program was about $1.0 billion, which led the oil giant to increase the offering to $800 million from $700 million, he said. The issue was led by J.P. Morgan.

Pemex also saw strong demand for its bankers acceptance facility led by Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd, which was also recently renewed. The program was initially set at about $425 million, but was increased to $460 million, Pemex said.
Both facilities matured in November, but were renewed recently due to favorable market conditions.

In September, Pemex renewed its U.S. commercial paper program, originally set for $400 million, lead bank Bank of America said in a release at the time. The issue was bumped up to $500 million on strong demand, in what was called the largest ever done by a Latin American issuer.
With the state-owned company focusing more on placing longer-dated notes, officials at Pemex said they do not see starting other short-term paper programs.
"In 1997, we will changing our orientation more towards capturing more medium and long term financing," Romero said.
That funding will be aimed at investment projects.
